positions.title: Queen mate

positions.title: The Saavedra position
positions.text: Only 1 c7 wins. Walk the king down the board to escape the checks, and when the pawn promotes, look out: a new queen would be met by a stalemate trick. Promote to the piece that still wins.

positions.title: Rook against pawn: stop it in time
positions.text: Your king is too far away to help, so the rook must do it alone. Only three moves win: get behind the pawn, cut the king off from it along a file, or attack the pawn along the rank. Anything slower lets the king escort its pawn home.

positions.title: Queen against a rook pawn
positions.text: With a rook pawn on the 7th and the white king far away, head for the corner: when the queen takes away your moves it is stalemate, so White can never bring the king closer.

positions.title: The wrong bishop
positions.text: Bishop and rook pawn cannot win when the queening square is the other colour from the bishop. Stay in the corner, or next to it, and never step out of it.

positions.title: Opposite-coloured bishops
positions.text: Control the square in front of the pawn with your bishop or king; the white bishop can never take it away.

positions.title: The right bishop

positions.title: Two connected pawns beat a rook
positions.text: Two connected passed pawns on the 6th rank beat a lone rook when the defending king is far away. Push them forward: the rook can't stop both, and you win it for a pawn.
